  // Phase 1: Technical Heuristics (Fail fast if it's an obvious headless browser)
  // Only cheap, synchronous signals that real readers never trip. Not used, on
  // purpose: navigator.plugins (empty on every Android Chrome and iOS browser)
  // and Permissions-API checks (they return a Promise, which is always truthy).
  const isObviousBot = () => {
    const ua = navigator.userAgent;
    return (
      navigator.webdriver === true || // W3C automation flag: Selenium, Puppeteer, Playwright
      // Named crawlers (Googlebot…) are already rejected by Umami's server-side
      // bot list; a generic /bot/ would also hit phone brands such as Cubot.
      /HeadlessChrome|PhantomJS|Lighthouse/.test(ua) ||
      window.callPhantom || window._phantom || // PhantomJS
      window.__nightmare || // Nightmare
      window.domAutomation || window.domAutomationController || // Chrome automation extension
      document.__selenium_unwrapped || document.__webdriver_evaluate || document.__driver_evaluate || // Selenium
      Object.keys(document).some((key) => /^\$(cdc|wdc)_/.test(key)) || // ChromeDriver's injected globals
      !navigator.languages || navigator.languages.length === 0 ||
      // Headless Chrome often lacks window.chrome. Android in-app browsers
      // (Facebook, Instagram…) are WebViews that lack it too, so they're excluded.
      (ua.includes('Chrome') && !ua.includes('; wv)') && !window.chrome)
    );
  };

  if (isObviousBot()) {
    return; // Silently exit, never track
  }

  // Phase 2: Proof of Life (Wait for human interaction)
  let hasTracked = false;
  
  const verifyHumanAndTrack = () => {
    if (hasTracked) return;
    
    // Ensure the Umami object is fully loaded before calling it
    if (window.umami && typeof window.umami.track === 'function') {
      hasTracked = true;
      
      // Trigger the standard pageview
      window.umami.track(); 
      
      // Cleanup: Remove listeners immediately so they don't impact scroll/paint performance
      ['mousemove', 'touchstart', 'keydown', 'scroll', 'wheel'].forEach(evt => 
        window.removeEventListener(evt, verifyHumanAndTrack, { capture: true })
      );
    }
  };

  // Attach passive listeners to catch the very first interaction
  // 'passive: true' ensures these listeners do not block the main thread or cause scroll lag
  ['mousemove', 'touchstart', 'keydown', 'scroll', 'wheel'].forEach(evt => 
    window.addEventListener(evt, verifyHumanAndTrack, { capture: true, once: true, passive: true })
  );

  // Optional Fallback: If a user loads an article and reads it for 10 seconds without touching the mouse/screen.
  // Only for a page someone is actually looking at, so background tabs and
  // unfocused automated pages that merely sit for 10s are not counted.
  setTimeout(() => {
    if (!hasTracked && window.umami && document.visibilityState === 'visible' && document.hasFocus()) {

    <script>(function() {
  // Phase 1: Technical Heuristics (Fail fast if it's an obvious headless browser)
  // Only cheap, synchronous signals that real readers never trip. Not used, on
  // purpose: navigator.plugins (empty on every Android Chrome and iOS browser)
  // and Permissions-API checks (they return a Promise, which is always truthy).
  const isObviousBot = () => {
    const ua = navigator.userAgent;
    return (
      navigator.webdriver === true || // W3C automation flag: Selenium, Puppeteer, Playwright
      // Named crawlers (Googlebot…) are already rejected by Umami's server-side
      // bot list; a generic /bot/ would also hit phone brands such as Cubot.
      /HeadlessChrome|PhantomJS|Lighthouse/.test(ua) ||
      window.callPhantom || window._phantom || // PhantomJS
      window.__nightmare || // Nightmare
      window.domAutomation || window.domAutomationController || // Chrome automation extension
      document.__selenium_unwrapped || document.__webdriver_evaluate || document.__driver_evaluate || // Selenium
      Object.keys(document).some((key) => /^\$(cdc|wdc)_/.test(key)) || // ChromeDriver's injected globals
      !navigator.languages || navigator.languages.length === 0 ||
      // Headless Chrome often lacks window.chrome. Android in-app browsers
      // (Facebook, Instagram…) are WebViews that lack it too, so they're excluded.
      (ua.includes('Chrome') && !ua.includes('; wv)') && !window.chrome)
    );
  };

  if (isObviousBot()) {
    return; // Silently exit, never track
  }

  // Phase 2: Proof of Life (Wait for human interaction)
  let hasTracked = false;
  
  const verifyHumanAndTrack = () => {
    if (hasTracked) return;
    
    // Ensure the Umami object is fully loaded before calling it
    if (window.umami && typeof window.umami.track === 'function') {
      hasTracked = true;
      
      // Trigger the standard pageview
      window.umami.track();

      ['mousemove', 'touchstart', 'keydown', 'scroll', 'wheel'].forEach(evt => 
        window.removeEventListener(evt, verifyHumanAndTrack, { capture: true })
      );
    }
  };

  // Attach passive listeners to catch the very first interaction
  // 'passive: true' ensures these listeners do not block the main thread or cause scroll lag
  ['mousemove', 'touchstart', 'keydown', 'scroll', 'wheel'].forEach(evt => 
    window.addEventListener(evt, verifyHumanAndTrack, { capture: true, once: true, passive: true })
  );

  // unfocused automated pages that merely sit for 10s are not counted.

  // Only cheap, synchronous signals that real readers never trip. Not used, on
  // purpose: navigator.plugins (empty on every Android Chrome and iOS browser)
  // and Permissions-API checks (they return a Promise, which is always truthy).
  const isObviousBot = () => {
    const ua = navigator.userAgent;
    return (
      navigator.webdriver === true || // W3C automation flag: Selenium, Puppeteer, Playwright
      // Named crawlers (Googlebot…) are already rejected by Umami's server-side
      // bot list; a generic /bot/ would also hit phone brands such as Cubot.
      /HeadlessChrome|PhantomJS|Lighthouse/.test(ua) ||
      window.callPhantom || window._phantom || // PhantomJS
      window.__nightmare || // Nightmare
      window.domAutomation || window.domAutomationController || // Chrome automation extension
      document.__selenium_unwrapped || document.__webdriver_evaluate || document.__driver_evaluate || // Selenium
      Object.keys(document).some((key) => /^\$(cdc|wdc)_/.test(key)) || // ChromeDriver's injected globals

      // (Facebook, Instagram…) are WebViews that lack it too, so they're excluded.

    if (hasTracked) return;

  // 'passive: true' ensures these listeners do not block the main thread or cause scroll lag

    window.addEventListener(evt, verifyHumanAndTrack, { capture: true, once: true, passive: true })

  const isObviousBot = () => {
